en.q:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I : Like nitrogen that can form ammonia, arsenic can form arsine.
Statement II : Antimony cannot form antimony pentoxide.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
en.sol: Statement I ✓: all group 15 elements form hydrides EH3 (NH3, PH3, AsH3 arsine, SbH3, BiH3). Statement II ✗: antimony does form Sb2O5 (group 15 elements form E2O3 and E2O5).
en.hint: Group 15 elements form EH<sub>3</sub>, E<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> and E<sub>2</sub>O<sub>5</sub>.

en.q:
Match List-I with List-II
List-I: (A) XeO3 (B) XeF2 (C) XeOF4 (D) XeF6
List-II: (I) sp3d; linear (II) sp3; pyramidal (III) sp3d3; distorted octahedral (IV) sp3d2; square pyramidal
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
en.sol:
• XeO3: 3 bond pairs + 1 lone pair → sp3, pyramidal (II).
  • XeF2: 2 bp + 3 lp → sp3d, linear (I).
  • XeOF4: 5 bp + 1 lp → sp3d2, square pyramidal (IV).
  • XeF6: 6 bp + 1 lp → sp3d3, distorted octahedral (III).
en.hint: Count bond pairs + lone pairs on Xe.

en.q:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The boiling point of hydrides of Group 16 elements follow the order H2O > H2Te > H2Se > H2S.
Statement II: On the basis of molecular mass, H2O is expected to have lower boiling point than the other members of the group but due to the presence of extensive H-bonding in H2O, it has higher boiling point.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
en.sol: Boiling points: H2O (373 K) > H2Te > H2Se > H2S. From H2S to H2Te the b.p. rises with molar mass (stronger van der Waals forces); H2O is far higher because of extensive hydrogen bonding. Both statements are true.
en.hint: H<sub>2</sub>O is the exception because of H-bonding.

hi.q:
नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:
कथन I: वर्ग 16 के तत्वों के हाइड्राइडों के क्वथनांक H2O > H2Te > H2Se > H2S क्रम का पालन करते हैं।
कथन II: आण्विक द्रव्यमान के आधार पर H2O का क्वथनांक वर्ग के अन्य सदस्यों से कम होने की अपेक्षा है परंतु H2O में व्यापक H-आबंधन की उपस्थिति के कारण इसका क्वथनांक अधिक है।
उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनिए:
o: कथन I और कथन II दोनों सत्य हैं
कथन I और कथन II दोनों असत्य हैं
कथन I सत्य है परंतु कथन II असत्य है
कथन I असत्य है परंतु कथन II सत्य है
hi.sol: क्वथनांक: H2O (373 K) > H2Te > H2Se > H2S। H2S से H2Te तक क्वथनांक मोलर द्रव्यमान के साथ बढ़ता है (प्रबल वांडरवाल्स बल); व्यापक हाइड्रोजन आबंधन के कारण H2O का क्वथनांक बहुत अधिक है। दोनों कथन सत्य हैं।

en.q: Among Group 16 elements, which one does NOT show −2 oxidation state?
en.sol: Down group 16 the stability of the −2 state falls. Polonium (metallic, most electropositive) hardly shows −2; its common states are +2 and +4.

en.q: Identify the incorrect statement from the following:
o: Phosphorus, arsenic and antimony show catenation property
P(C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>5</sub>)<sub>3</sub> and As(C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>5</sub>)<sub>3</sub> form dπ − dπ bond with transition metals
Nitrogen can form dπ − pπ bond with oxygen
Nitrogen can form pπ − pπ multiple bonds with itself.
en.sol: Nitrogen has no d orbitals, so it cannot form dπ–pπ bonds (unlike P, which forms dπ–pπ bonds with O). Statement (3) is incorrect. P, As, Sb show (weak) catenation; P and As compounds such as PEt3 and AsPh3 form dπ–dπ bonds with transition metals; N forms pπ–pπ multiple bonds (N≡N).
en.hint: Second-period element → no d orbitals.

en.q: Noble gases are named because of their inertness towards reactivity. Identify an incorrect statement about them.
o: Noble gases have large positive values of electron gain enthalpy
Noble gases are sparingly soluble in water
Noble gases have very high melting and boiling points
Noble gases have weak dispersion forces
en.sol: Noble gases have only weak dispersion forces between atoms, so their melting and boiling points are very low. Statement (3) is incorrect. They have large positive electron gain enthalpies (stable configuration) and are sparingly soluble in water.
en.hint: Weak forces → low boiling points.

en.q: In which one of the following arrangements the given sequence is not strictly according to the properties indicated against it?
o: CO<sub>2</sub> < SiO<sub>2</sub> < SnO<sub>2</sub> < PbO<sub>2</sub> : Increasing oxidizing power
HF < HCl < HBr < HI : Increasing acidic strength
H<sub>2</sub>O < H<sub>2</sub>S < H<sub>2</sub>Se < H<sub>2</sub>Te : Increasing pK<sub>a</sub> values
NH<sub>3</sub> < PH<sub>3</sub> < AsH<sub>3</sub> < SbH<sub>3</sub> : Increasing acidic character
en.sol: Acid strength of H2E increases down group 16 (H–E bond weakens): H2O < H2S < H2Se < H2Te. Stronger acid → lower pKa, so the pKa values decrease in this order. Sequence (3) is wrong. (1) oxidising power rises down group 14 (inert pair effect), (2) HF < HCl < HBr < HI acidity ✓, (4) ✓ as keyed.
en.hint: Higher acidity means smaller pK<sub>a</sub>.
